data.description:
# The Gerrit review bot cannot invoke Bedrock: LLM-Review fail-closes on every change

Since the eb6e Bedrock cutover went live, the review bot's `base` step dies with a 403 and the
bot casts a fail-closed `LLM-Review -1`. **Nothing can land through Gerrit** — the `LLM-Review +1`
gate is one of the two required votes and only the bot can cast it.

## Evidence

Change 1331, patch set 1 (2026-08-04 00:45:54Z):

    [LLM-Review: BLOCK — coverage-gap (llm-unavailable)]
    step 'base' failed: status_code: 403, model_name: us.anthropic.claude-opus-4-8
    User: arn:aws:sts::896586841071:assumed-role/rebar-gerrit-instance-role/i-00880b2c7f13527c5
    is not authorized to perform: bedrock:InvokeModel on resource:
    arn:aws:bedrock:us-east-1:896586841071:inference-profile/us.anthropic.claude-opus-4-8
    with an explicit deny in an identity-based policy

    Automatic retries exhausted (1 attempt(s)) — casting the fail-closed -1.

## It is a regression, and the window is tight

 * change 1330 got `LLM-Review +1` at **00:28:44Z** — the bot was healthy.
 * change 1331 got the 403 at **00:45:54Z**.

The cutover (`eb6e`, merged as `5892134975`) fills `REBAR_LLM_FRONTIER_MODEL` with
`bedrock:us.anthropic.claude-opus-4-8` in `infra/compose/docker-compose.yml:186`. The review
gate's `base` step is the `frontier` class, so it is the first thing the cutover re-points and
the first thing to hit the deny.

## What I ruled out — the deny is NOT in the role

Read the instance role directly (`joe_frontier`, same account 896586841071):

 * inline `rebar-gerrit-bedrock-converse` **ALLOWS** `bedrock:InvokeModel` on
   `arn:aws:bedrock:*:896586841071:inference-profile/*.anthropic.claude-*`, which matches the
   requested resource, and on `arn:aws:bedrock:*::foundation-model/anthropic.claude-*`.
 * the other two inline policies (`rebar-gerrit-cloudwatch-basic`, `rebar-gerrit-ssm-params-read`)
   contain no `Deny` and no bedrock action.
 * the only attached managed policy is `AmazonSSMManagedInstanceCore`.
 * `PermissionsBoundary: None`.

So there is **no deny anywhere in this role's identity policies**. The explicit deny is being
applied from outside the role — an org-level SCP or a similar account-wide guardrail — which is
why it cannot be fixed by editing the role.

**CI's Bedrock access is unaffected**, which localises it further: the `external LLM (live
bedrock)` arm of run 30857265932 succeeded at 22:04Z under the separate
`rebar-external-ci-bedrock` role. Only the Gerrit instance role is denied.

## Two candidate fixes (needs an operator decision — I did not act on production infra)

 1. **Amend the org/SCP guardrail** to permit `bedrock:InvokeModel` on the opus-4-8 inference
    profile for `rebar-gerrit-instance-role`. Requires AWS admin.
 2. **Pull the documented kill switch** — `docker-compose.yml:160-163` records it as purely
    subtractive: delete the three `REBAR_LLM_*_MODEL` lines and recreate the container, and rebar
    resolves the classes back to the direct-Anthropic defaults. Restores reviews immediately;
    reverts the cutover's benefit. Needs SSM/SSH to the Gerrit host.

A third, narrower option if only opus is denied: re-point `REBAR_LLM_FRONTIER_MODEL` at the
sonnet profile that the standard class already uses — but that is unverified, because the deny's
source is unknown and may cover every Claude profile for this role. Do not assume it is
opus-only without testing.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] the source of the explicit deny is identified and named
- [ ] a change pushed to Gerrit receives a real `LLM-Review` verdict (not `llm-unavailable`)
- [ ] whichever fix is chosen, the outcome is recorded here with the change/run that proves it
data.title: Gerrit review bot 403s on Bedrock: LLM-Review fail-closes on every change, nothing can land
